newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end lower, shrug off Deng's death.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end lower, shrug off Deng's death.

text.p: A lack of details on a hoped-for early expansion of the foreign stock investment ceiling pushed Seoul stocks to close lower on Thursday, brokers said.
They said the market was not affected by the death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping.
The composite stock index shed 2.54 points to 711.13, off a day high of 716.18. Losers led gainers by 429 to 357.

"Many investors stayed on the sidelines as no further news on the foreign stock limit was given," said Kim Duck-sun of Hyundai Securities. "Consolidation will prevail this week. But no big falls of the index are expected," he added.

A government official said on Tuesday the government was considering further relaxation of foreign stock investment limit as a way to slow the won's decline against the dollar. But no exact date has been set. "The market is waiting for the announcement," said a Samsung Securities analyst.

He said the market was concerned that foreign investors have become net sellers. Foreigners liquidated financial shares, turning instead to manufacturing shares including electronics, memory chips and chemical companies. LG Semicon rose 800 won to 25,600 and Hyundai Electronics was unchanged at 32,400, up from a low of 31,200.
Hanjin Heavy hit its upper limit of 500 won to close at 6,800 on active foreign buying.

Sporadic buying also remained strong in pharmaceuticals and shares targetted by mergers and acquisitions talk. Korea Green Cross went limit up, gaining 5,600 won to 75,600 and Yuhan Corp added 1,700 won to 47,600.
"Market liquidity still looks good. But with no specific leading shares, the market will drift sideways due to uncertainty over the market direction," Kim said.
